prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one universal “best” — the right company depends on your exact location, roof type, budget and whether you need a Class 4/impact or HVHZ (High Velocity Hurricane Zone) installation. Instead of naming a single company, here’s a practical way to find the best hurricane-rated roofer in Miami and what to require from them.

What to require (must-haves)
- Florida-certified roofing contractor (check Florida DBPR license).  
- Proof of general liability and workers’ compensation insurance.  
- Experience installing hurricane-rated systems and components (HVHZ details if your area is in the HVHZ).  
- Familiarity with and use of Miami-Dade County product approvals/NOAs for materials and assemblies.  
- Manufacturer-certified installer status (so you get full manufacturer warranty).  
- Written, itemized estimate and a clear contract with scope, materials, permit responsibility, timeline, payment schedule, and cleanup.  
- Permit pulled in your name (or contractor’s) and final inspection required.  
- Written workmanship warranty in addition to manufacturer warranty.

Key technical items to confirm
- Use of Miami-Dade NOA-approved products (shingles, underlayment, fasteners).  
- Proper roof deck attachment and hurricane straps/ties as required by code.  
- Secondary water barrier (synthetic underlayment or ice & water shield) and adequate ventilation.  
- Correct fastener pattern (many manufacturers require 6 nails in HVHZ instead of 4).  
- Impact-rated (Class 4) shingles or specified metal system if you want impact resistance.  
- Engineering and structural upgrades if needed (to meet wind uplift requirements).

How to find and vet top contractors
1. Get at least 3 bids from local roofers who specialize in hurricane-rated work.  
2. Verify the contractor’s Florida license on the DBPR site and confirm insurance certificates with your insurance agent.  
3. Ask for recent local references and photos of completed hurricane-rated installs. Call the references.  
4. Check Miami-Dade County NOA listings for the exact products the contractor proposes.  
5. Read BBB, Google, Yelp, Nextdoor reviews — watch for recent patterns of complaints.  
6. Avoid “storm chasers” (contractors who solicit aggressively after a storm, pressure you to sign quickly, or require full upfront payment).  
7. Require a written permit and final inspection — don’t pay final balance until you have a certificate of completion/inspection.

Questions to ask every contractor
- Are you licensed and insured? What’s your license number?  
- Are you an approved installer for the manufacturer of the roofing material?  
- Which Miami-Dade NOA-approved products and assemblies will you use? Can you show the NOA?  
- How will the roof be attached to resist wind uplift? (Describe straps, fasteners, pattern.)  
- Who pulls the permit and who will do inspections?  
- What is the warranty (manufacturer and workmanship)? Is it transferable?  
- Can I see 3 recent local references and photos of finished jobs?

If you want, I can:
- Narrow this to a short list of well-reviewed Miami roofers if you give your ZIP code.  
- Provide a sample checklist/contract addendum you can give contractors.  

Which would you prefer?
